🎟️ Parlays & round robins — 8 tickets

Each ticket opens to show what it is, why it's on the card, and every leg.

💡 "(est.)" price: each leg's odds multiplied together, the standard way to estimate what a parlay pays. The book's actual payout can differ a little, and same-game parlays (several legs from one game) pay noticeably less because the legs are related. Check the payout on your slip.

🛡️ How the night-game hedge works (read this first)
  • Why the last leg is a night game. These parlays end with the moneyline favorite in the Sunday-night (or Monday-night) game. That leg is a placeholder: it keeps the ticket alive until night so that, if the morning and afternoon legs all win, you still have a decision to make.
  • Locking in a profit. Once only the night leg is left, bet the underdog in that same game. Size the bet so you come out ahead whichever team wins: if the favorite wins, the parlay pays; if the underdog wins, the hedge pays. Each ticket below shows the stake and the profit it locks at today's prices.
  • Finding a middle. Instead of the underdog moneyline, you can hedge with the underdog plus the points. If the favorite wins but by less than the spread, both bets win. Middles are uncommon, but they are the best outcome on these tickets. If the underdog wins outright, the hedge still covers you.
  • What it costs. The hedge is a bigger second bet, often ten times the parlay stake, and prices will have moved by the night game, so recalculate first. Hedging part of the way is fine if you want to keep some upside.
  • The formula. Hedge stake = what the parlay pays back (stake included) ÷ the hedge bet's decimal odds. Profit locked = parlay payback − parlay stake − hedge stake.

Build rules from the season record:

#RuleEvidence (season, unique legs)
1No −120 to −100 connector legs unless sourcing tier 1–2 (Section 4). Take −121 or longer, or plus money.31-45-1, 41% vs 53% needed, −23% (n=76), bad both weeks
2Underdog spreads are allowed when the matchup and price case are stated. Do not use points merely to make a parlay leg feel safer.Week 1 spread dogs were 10-20, −44%; that is a review signal, not a prohibition.
3Lean on tackles+assists and passing TDs. Keep sacks and receiving yards to a minimum.T+A 9-4 +22%, pass TD 8-3 +14%; rec yds −27%, receptions −18%, sacks 2-3
4Props go on the side you expect to win. Never stack an offense you fade elsewhere on the card.56% vs 39% (Week 2)
5Each starting QB is one shared risk across every leg on his offense. Count those legs as one exposure.MNF Dart injury: Giants legs 4-15
6ML chalk ≤ −290 is not a free anchor. Flag it; one per ticket at most.6-4 vs ~78% implied; TB −410, BAL −379, LAC −292 all lost
7Structure: 2-leg tickets and 2-team RRs first. Straight parlays of 5+ legs are moonshots only ($5, one or two a week).All 3 Week 2 winners were 2-leg or 2-team; 5+ leg straights 0-26
8Receptions are tight to the line. Only for proven target share on the expected winner. Yardage is bimodal, so don't pay −110 to −120 for a median line.9 of 12 rec losses were within 1.5 catches
9Moonshot ATD stacks lose. One long-priced TD (+150 or longer) is fine as a single or in an RR.ATD moonshots 0-11 on scorers; +150-or-longer band +20%
10Bookmaker vs BetOnline: no edge either way (50% vs 49% after the 9/22 book correction). Choose the book by rule and price, not habit.—

7. What the Experts Say: Consensus & Clashes

What the experts are saying, counted fairly. We collect picks from betting podcasts, YouTube shows and betting writers, then count each source once per game on the side it picked most. A lopsided count (for example 6–1) means broad agreement; a clash means credible sources are split. The table ranks games from the strongest agreement down.

📖 How to read this section
  • Source: one outlet, podcast host or writer. Outlets that publish several writers (ESPN, VSiN) still count as one vote.
  • For – Against: sources backing the consensus side vs. the other side. Ties inside one source are dropped.
  • Strength (the table is ordered by this first): 🌟 Near-unanimous = at least 3× as many sources on one side, or none against · 🔥 Majority = ahead by 2 or more · ⚔️ Clash = ahead by only 1 · ⚖️ Split = dead even.
  • Total lean: whether more sources picked the Over or the Under.
  • Agreement is not a guarantee. Heavy consensus on a popular side can already be priced into the line; see the big-money column in Section 6.

📖 Game script

With Jaxson Dart on IR, Jameis Winston (211+ passing) starts for the Giants, who score 15.3 points a game and are also missing pass rusher Brian Burns. Arizona has a HIGH secondary grade here (severity 7.32): Jacoby Brissett (231+; 38 of 52 for 280 last week) throws to Trey McBride (64+, +151 to score) and Marvin Harrison Jr., and Jeremiyah Love (67+ rushing, −136 to score) takes the work with James Conner out. New York's path is Malik Nabers (57+) on a MEDIUM grade and Najee Harris near the goal line (Sean Koerner, +330). Arizona by four, covering −2.5; 44 total.

🧠 Why the card leans this way

The line flipped five points, from the Action Network open of NYG −2.5 to ARI −2.5, on the Dart news. ARI: Chad Millman (on Arizona early), Sharp or Square (+1.5 before the flip) and BettingPros on the moneyline ("Winston is unreliable as a market favorite"). NYG: Brandon Anderson (+2.5, "the line shouldn't have flipped this much"), Steve Makinen of VSiN (+2.5, "not sure the right team is favored here"), Matt Moore (+1.5 contest pick), Steve Fezzik and Ross Tucker teasing NYG to +7.5, and Mike Florio (Giants 23–17). The two contest picks are at the contest's +1.5. Andrew Erickson ("stay away") and Dave Tuley both pass. Money agrees with the move: ARI has 62% of spread tickets and 69% of the money, and the ARI moneyline is a big-money flag (62% of tickets, 78% of money). The lean is ARI −2.5 or the −143 moneyline. On the total, Action Network has over 44.5 and Zachary Cohen of VSiN has Jameis Winston's passing overs; Evan Abrams' primer notes Winston is 17–6 to the over in October in his career, while a wind-under system points the other way. The projection is half a point under, so pass the total; Winston's passing yards are the better angle. Card: the ARI moneyline anchors the Slot 3 Morning parlay, the Slot 5 Hybrid and the 2-leg ARI ML + JAX ML ticket; ARI −1.5 is a proposed SuperContest pick (both SuperContest tickets). The 7a Morning prop stack carries Jacoby Brissett 2+ passing TDs and a Jameis Winston interception.

⚠️ What breaks it

Winston's volatility cuts both ways: two long Nabers plays put the Giants ahead. Brissett has thrown 52 times in a game, and turnovers on that volume would hand New York the short field. There's a 53% chance of second-half showers (NWS), which would slow both passing games.

📖 Game script

San Francisco is without Nick Bosa and Mykel Williams (both out), with Mike Evans questionable. Brock Purdy (234+) leans on Christian McCaffrey: 66+ rushing, −245 to score, and Warren Sharp and PropStarz both take his receiving over because Denver blitzes at one of the highest early-down rates and Purdy checks down against it. George Kittle (65+) adds to that. Denver: Bo Nix (223+), J.K. Dobbins (60+, +118 to score), Courtland Sutton (Gilles Gallant, +240 to score) and Jaylen Waddle (57+) on a MEDIUM grade. It's about 90°F at kickoff. The 49ers score 32.7 a game at 7.3 yards per play, so this is close. San Francisco by one: Denver covers +2.5, and 47 points goes under 48.

🧠 Why the card leans this way

This is the most one-sided expert game on the slate. DEN: Action Network, Sharp or Square, Steve Fezzik, BettingPros, Chad Millman (his "trade of the week," calling the reverse line move sharp), John Jastremski, Evan Abrams, Matt Moore, Andrew Erickson (+3) and Dave Tuley of VSiN (+8.5 in teasers, a best bet). SF: Mike Florio (49ers 24–20) and Steve Makinen of VSiN (−3, a best bet). Splits: SF has 60% of spread tickets and 64% of the money and 84% of moneyline tickets, yet the line came down from the Action Network open of SF −3 to −2.5. Every DEN +3 position is now +2.5, past the key number. The lean is DEN +2.5 or the +126 moneyline, plus McCaffrey receiving. On the total, 60% of the money is on the under against 52% of tickets, and the total is up from 45.5 to 48; small under lean. Card: the heaviest exposure on the card (about $85). The DEN moneyline is in the Slot 2 Dog-ML 2-team RR, the Slot 4 Afternoon parlay and the Slot 5 Hybrid; DEN +2.5 is a proposed SuperContest pick (both SuperContest tickets); DEN +8.5 is a leg of the 6-pt Wong teaser JAX-DEN-ATL. A 49ers win by 3 or more hurts six tickets at once.

⚠️ What breaks it

The 49ers' offense, at 63% on third down, doesn't need Bosa to win a shootout: Kittle and McCaffrey beat the blitz and San Francisco wins by ten. Denver scores only 20 a game and can't keep pace if Nix is pressured. Mike Evans is a game-time decision with a rib injury (ESPN); recheck at the 11:55 PT inactive window.

Indianapolis by six: a cover of −4.5 by a point and a half, 46 total points.

The projection (IND by 6) and the 7–4 expert lean to Washington point opposite ways, so the card passes the side and the receiving props.

Mariota runs well and Croskey-Merritt controls the clock, holding the Colts to field goals. McLaurin plays through the doubtful tag. Indianapolis is −5 in turnover margin through three games, so two giveaways turn a six-point Colts win into a Washington cover. Recheck inactives at about 05:00 PT.

The Jaguars allow 12 points a game and are +4 in turnovers; the Bengals allow 21. Cincinnati by two: Jacksonville covers +2.5, and the 52 points land on the total.

🧠 Why the card leans this way

Experts split 6–4. JAX: Action Network, Brandon Kravitz (The Favorites), Doug Kezirian, and three teasers through +8.5 (Steve Fezzik and Ross Tucker of Even Money, and Dave Tuley's VSiN best bet). One counterweight from Evan Abrams' primer: teams covering by 10-plus points a game over their first three (the Jaguars this week) are 47–72–3 against the spread in their next game over 15 seasons. The line has held at CIN −2.5 since the Action Network open; the total went up from 50.5 to 52. The lean is JAX +2.5, or the +129 moneyline, and JAX +8.5 as a Wong teaser leg through 3 and 7. Jacksonville's +4 turnover margin regresses and Burrow gets a clean pocket all day; Chase hits two explosives and Cincinnati wins by a touchdown. If the moneyline money keeps coming and the line flips to JAX, the price is gone.

Minnesota is 3–0 because of its defense: 13.7 points allowed and a 22.7% third-down rate allowed under Brian Flores. The offense gains only 4.3 yards per play, and Justin Jefferson is out. Aaron Jones Sr. (−200 to score at BetOnline), Jordan Addison and T.J. Hockenson carry the offense. Miami is without De'Von Achane; Malik Willis (170+ passing) throws to Malik Washington (39+) and Chris Bell (35+), with Jaylen Wright (29+) in the backfield. It's a fixed-roof stadium. Minnesota by eight, so Miami covers +10; 36 points, under 38.5.

🧠 Why the card leans this way

The line went from the Action Network open of MIN −10.5 to −10, and the total from 42.5 to 38.5. The lean is MIA +10. The under is the right side but four points are already gone; Action Network's Evan likes Willis' rushing over as the prop. Card: Single MIA +10 ($15) is the biggest single, MIA +10 is also in the Slot 5 Hybrid, and MIA +10.5 is a proposed SuperContest pick (book +10 on both SuperContest tickets). The 7b Afternoon prop stack carries a Malik Willis interception, a deliberate partial hedge against the MIA spread.

⚠️ What breaks it

Minnesota's defense scores, or Willis turns it over twice under pressure from Flores, and the Vikings win by 14. If Murray doesn't start, Minnesota's offense gets even thinner, which helps the under and the Miami cover but adds noise. Recheck at the 11:35 PT inactive window.

New England averages 12 points with a −5 turnover margin; Drake Maye leans on Hunter Henry and Romeo Doubs (40+) on the MEDIUM side. Chicago starts Tyson Bagent (Bookmaker's 201+ passing line is his) with Caleb Williams out. The Bears' offense (29.7 points and 184 rushing yards a game) runs through D'Andre Swift (64+ rushing, −136 to score) and Colston Loveland (35+). New York is without Breece Hall and Mason Taylor (both out), with Kenyon Sadiq questionable, so Braelon Allen (57+ rushing, +118 to score) carries and Geno Smith throws to Garrett Wilson (78+ at −105) on a HIGH-graded matchup against a Chicago secondary missing a cornerback and a safety (both out). The Jets' defense allows 258 yards a game, which keeps it close. Chicago by three, so New York covers +3.5 on the hook; 43 points, on the total.

🧠 Why the card leans this way

The named experts favor New York on price: Steve Fezzik and Ross Tucker (Even Money, both at +3.5), Action Network's contest pick, BettingPros at +3, Wes Reynolds of VSiN (+3.5) and Kendra Middleton ("an even better spot if Bagent starts"). The CHI side is Mike Florio (Bears 27–17), Andrew Erickson's BettingPros primer (−3.5) and a BettingPros pick at −3.5 that was written around Case Keenum starting. Dave Tuley of VSiN passes. ESPN and Pro Football Talk both report that Bagent is expected to start, the condition Kendra Middleton named. Splits lean Chicago, 57% of tickets and 62% of money, no sharp gap; the NYJ moneyline has 13% of tickets and 18% of money. The line went from the Action Network open of CHI −3 to −3.5. The lean is NYJ +3.5 for the hook; the projection lands on the 43 total, and the only total signal is a wind-under system in Evan Abrams' primer, so no total. ⚠️ What breaks it

Keenum starts instead of Bagent, which is the case the BettingPros CHI pick rests on, and the Bears pass better than this script assumes. Chicago's 59-point opener shows the ceiling. A Jets turnover in their own end flips a three-point game into a seven-point one. If the number drops back to −3, the hook is gone and so is the lean.

📖 Game script

Baltimore comes back from Brazil with Ethan Pocic and a guard out, Ronnie Stanley questionable, Trey Hendrickson out and Zay Flowers questionable. Rain is likely for the first half (NWS 62–75%). Derrick Henry (98+ rushing, −245 to score, the shortest on the board) carries the revenge game, and Dave expects Lamar Jackson under 27.5 attempts. Tennessee scores 12.3 points a game; Cam Ward has Calvin Ridley on a MEDIUM grade and Tony Pollard (48+; PropStarz over 45.5) on the ground. The Ravens build an early lead and the Titans close the gap late. Baltimore by ten, so Tennessee covers +11.5; 42 points.

🧠 Why the card leans this way

TEN: Steve Fezzik ("best bet"), Ross Tucker (2 units) Kendra Middleton (the Ravens' long flight home and injuries) and Dave Tuley of VSiN (a best bet). BAL: Brandon Anderson (−11.5 and his contest pick), BettingPros, Sharp or Square (first half only, to avoid a second-half backdoor) and Mike Florio (Ravens 30–17). Splits: BAL has 66% of spread tickets and 71% of the money, but the TEN moneyline is a big-money flag, 4% of tickets and 19% of the money. Evan Abrams' primer has two systems on Tennessee (fading no-pedigree favorites, and fading the public after a poor offensive game), and Baltimore's starting center is out for two to three months. The line is unchanged from the Action Network open at −11.5; the total is down from 43.5 to 43. The lean is TEN +11.5, or BAL first half as Sharp or Square plays it; both fit a script where Baltimore leads early and Tennessee covers late. BettingPros (43.5) and Andrew Erickson (42.5) have the over, but with rain and a projected 42 the total is a pass. Card: the TEN moneyline (+492) is the long leg of the Slot 2 Dog-ML 2-team RR, and TEN +11.5 is a proposed SuperContest pick (both SuperContest tickets). Derrick Henry 2+ TDs is in the 8b 2+ TD 3-leg.

⚠️ What breaks it

The patched Baltimore line holds, Henry gets 30 carries and the Ravens win by 17. Ward turns it over twice (Sharp or Square calls him regressing). Flowers plays a full game and stretches the field Tennessee is trying to shrink.

🎙️ What the experts are saying

Tennessee side.

Steve Fezzik (Even Money): TEN +11.5, his best bet, a contest pick and 1 unit: "Baltimore got gifted their last game" and "has a long travel turnaround."

Total. BettingPros has over 43.5: "Cam Ward pushes overs on the road." Andrew Erickson has over 42.5.

Props. PropStarz has Zay Flowers over 67.5 ("practiced in full") and Tony Pollard over 45.5 rushing against "a putrid Ravens run defense." EC has Wan'Dale Robinson over 37.5. Dave has Lamar Jackson under 27.5 pass attempts. Grant Neiffer has Pollard to score at +205 and Jackson at +250. Sal Bets has Derrick Henry over 105.5 total yards.

What the betting lines are predicting. Every point spread and total is really a forecast. Put the two together and you get the final score the sportsbook expects; the moneylines give each team's chance of winning. Next to that is our own projected score (from the game write-ups in Section 6) and where the bets and the money are landing, on both sides of every market.

📖 What each column means (plain English)
  • Favorite & spread: the team expected to win and by how many points. "BUF −7" means Buffalo has to win by 8 or more for a Buffalo spread bet to cash.
  • Total points: the combined score the sportsbook set as its over/under line.
  • Score the lines imply: the final score the spread and total point to together. Example: total 50.5 and BUF −7 → Buffalo about 28.8, Chargers about 21.8.
  • Our projection: Platinum Rose's own projected final: the line, adjusted for injuries, matchups, expert opinion and money moves. Not a computer-model output.
  • Win chance: each moneyline turned into a win probability, with the sportsbook's built-in cut removed so the two sides add up to 100%.
  • Spread / Total (bets / money): for each side, the share of bets placed and the share of dollars wagered. Example: "O 25/51 · U 75/49" means only 25% of bets are on the Over but they carry 51% of the money.
  • 💰 Big-money signal: a side where the money share beats the bet share by 15+ points — fewer, bigger bets, usually experienced ("sharp") bettors. We record the exact line when the signal first appears, so later builds show whether the line has moved toward or away from that side since.

📖 How the stars work
  • Stars show how much evidence lines up behind a bet, compared with our other bets this week. More stars = a stronger case. They are not a win percentage.
  • Where a bet starts: ★★★½ when our own matchup numbers and at least two named experts back it · ★★★ when our matchup numbers back it · ★★½ when at least two named experts picked it · ★★ when the support is only partial.
  • Up half a star when the experts are lopsided in its favor (at least four of them, two-to-one or better), or when the big-money bettors are on the same side.
  • Down half a star when more experts picked the other side, when the big money is on the other side, or when an injury or lineup question is still open.
  • We do not use a computer model's win percentage here: ours failed its accuracy test, so it is left out.

5. Survivor Pool Picks: Safest Teams This Week

Survivor pools: pick one team to win each week; you cannot use a team twice, and one loss usually ends your run. So the best pick balances three things: how likely the team is to win, how many others in your pool are on the same team (if a popular pick loses, much of the field goes with it), and whether you would rather save the team for a better spot later.

3. Teaser Bets: 6-Point Wong Teasers

📖 What a 6-point Wong teaser is (tap to read)

What a teaser is: you move the point spread 6 points in your favor on every leg, in exchange for a smaller payout, and every leg must win. The "Wong" version only uses lines where those 6 points cross both 3 and 7, the two most common NFL winning margins: favorites of −7.5 to −8.5 (teased down to −1.5 / −2.5) and underdogs of +1.5 to +2.5 (teased up to +7.5 / +8.5). Keep teasers to 2 legs.

The card plays 6-pt Wong teaser JAX-DEN-ATL as one 3-team teaser. A leg that opposes a side we are playing elsewhere (see above) is a hedge, not extra edge. The math is below.

Teaser math: 2, 3 and 4 legs, and round robins

Prices are the usual 6-point payouts (2-team −120, 3-team +160, 4-team +260); confirm BKR's on the slip. "Break-even per leg" is how often each leg must cover for the ticket to break even. Historically, Wong legs have covered roughly 72–75% of the time, but that is a long-run average, not a promise for this week's legs.

TicketBreak-even per legEV if legs cover 70%EV if legs cover 72%EV if legs cover 74%EV if legs cover 76%
2-team (−120)73.9%-10.2%-5.0%+0.4%+5.9%
3-team (+160)72.7%-10.8%-3.0%+5.4%+14.1%
4-team (+260)72.6%-13.6%-3.3%+8.0%+20.1%

What the table says: the edge per leg compounds. If the legs really cover 74% or better, bigger teasers return more per dollar; at 72% the 2-team loses and the 3- and 4-team are near break-even; at 70% all of them lose, the 4-team most. A round robin does not change the expected return per dollar of a single ticket of the same size; it trades some upside for a better chance of getting something back.

Structure ($1 per ticket, legs at 74%)TicketsEV per $Chance of a profit
3 legs by 2s3+0.4%41%
4 legs by 2s6+0.4%30%
4 legs by 3s4+5.4%30%
4-team straight1+8.0%30%
3-team straight1+5.4%41%

4. The Underdog Upset Ticket: The Dogs and Why

How it works: 6 underdogs to win outright, combined into every two-team parlay — 15 combos × $1.33, $19.95 total. Payout by number of winners: returns (avg): 2 hit $12, 3 hit $35, 4 hit $70, 5 hit $116, 6 hit $175. Two winners does not turn a profit on this build; it needs three or more. Each dog is on the ticket because we think its chance of winning is better than its price implies — not because we expect all of them to win.

🐶 Jacksonville Jaguars +129 — JAX@CIN · tier 2 · our projection JAX 25 – CIN 27

Why it's on the ticket: Experts split 6–4. JAX: Action Network, Brandon Kravitz (The Favorites), Doug Kezirian, and three teasers through +8.5 (Steve Fezzik and Ross Tucker of Even Money, and Dave Tuley's VSiN best bet). CIN: Sharp or Square ("prime bounce-back spot for Burrow"), Jason Radowitz of BettingPros, Steve Makinen of VSiN (a best bet) and Mike Florio (Bengals 28–27). The money is the story: the JAX moneyline has 38% of tickets but 58% of the money, a 20-point sharp gap, and JAX has 63% of spread tickets and 62% of the money. One counterweight from Evan Abrams' primer: teams covering by 10-plus points a game over their first three (the Jaguars this week) are 47–72–3 against the spread in their next game over 15 seasons. The line has held at CIN −2.5 since the Action Network open; the total went up from 50.5 to 52. The lean is JAX +2.5, or the +129 moneyline, and JAX +8.5 as a Wong teaser leg through 3 and 7. The over is the consensus (Andrew Erickson at 51, BettingPros at 50.5), but it has moved 1.5 points and the projection sits on the number, so play Parker Washington's receiving instead of the total. Card: the JAX moneyline is in the Slot 2 Dog-ML 2-team RR and the 2-leg ARI ML + JAX ML ticket, and JAX +8.5 is a leg of the 6-pt Wong teaser JAX-DEN-ATL.

What breaks it: Jacksonville's +4 turnover margin regresses and Burrow gets a clean pocket all day; Chase hits two explosives and Cincinnati wins by a touchdown. If the moneyline money keeps coming and the line flips to JAX, the price is gone.

Card evidence: Big-money flag (38% tickets / 58% money); 6–4 named experts JAX; projection CIN by 2 · full game write-up
